builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Joint Null-Space Projection for Data-Free Model Merging
summary: JNSP replaces entry-wise merging heuristics (averaging, TIES, Task Arithmetic) with a closed-form projection that removes from each task vector the components lying in other tasks' top-r right-singular subspaces. It costs one SVD per two-dimensional weight tensor per task, requires no data, forward passes, or training, and is order-independent, so it runs comfortably on constrained infrastructure. It can fail outside the validated setting: on RoBERTa-large it underperforms plain Task Arithmetic, and a sequential variant collapses to 69.6%, so the specific joint formulation matters.
rationale: The method is cheap, data-free, and shows large validated gains on CLIP vision models, but its demonstrated failure on an NLP backbone means the reader should validate it on their own checkpoints before adopting it in production.
technique: Joint null-space projection for model merging

claims.statement: JNSP replaces entry-wise merging heuristics (averaging, TIES, Task Arithmetic) with a closed-form projection that removes from each task vector the components lying in other tasks' top-r right-singular subspaces. It costs one SVD per two-dimensional weight tensor per task, requires no data, forward passes, or training, and is order-independent, so it runs comfortably on constrained infrastructure. It can fail outside the validated setting: on RoBERTa-large it underperforms plain Task Arithmetic, and a sequential variant collapses to 69.6%, so the specific joint formulation matters.

On eight CLIP tasks, merged ViT-B/16 reaches 89.45% average accuracy data-free, +11.88 points over TIES-Merging (77.57%) and +14.22 over Task Arithmetic; gains replicate across ViT-B/16, B/32, and L/14 (+10.8, +12.6, +9.1 over TIES).
